text:
sanjay: heads up — noticed a regression after yesterday's RBAC refactor. service accounts started getting 403 on kms:encrypt in the prod canary. key fetch failing in model-serving path. rolling back the refactor for the canary now.

maria: saw the same on staging around 14:02. app logs show `authorization error: missing permission kms:encrypt`. cloud audit shows KMS requests but actor metadata is weird (`actor_type` null).

ben: quick diagnose — the refactor removed the implicit role inheritance from `service-account` -> `kms-user`. migration step forgot to populate existing service account bindings. new role model expects explicit grants.

anne_ops: rolling back v2-rbac to previous canary. enabling verbose audit logging for KMS for the next 60 minutes. will follow up with logs in ~10m.

maria: sketched a migration script for the missing bindings. patch idea:
```sql
-- find service accounts that previously had kms scope (heuristic)
SELECT sa.id FROM service_accounts sa
LEFT JOIN role_bindings rb ON rb.subject_id = sa.id
WHERE rb.role IS NULL AND sa.scopes LIKE '%kms%';

-- insert implicit kms-user binding
INSERT INTO role_bindings (subject_id, role, created_by)
SELECT id, 'kms-user', 'rbac-migration-v2' FROM (
  SELECT sa.id as id FROM service_accounts sa
  LEFT JOIN role_bindings rb ON rb.subject_id = sa.id
  WHERE rb.role IS NULL AND sa.scopes LIKE '%kms%'
) s;
```

ben: that looks good. two safety items: add a dry-run mode and a timestamp tag so we can revert. e.g. `migration_tag = 'v2-rbac-implicit-kms-2026-03-20'`. also run on staging first.

maria: yup will add `--dry-run` and a `--revert-tag`. i'll open a small job in infra to run against staging tomorrow at 03:00 UTC.

sanjay: SDK note — the Python SDK change that introduced `require_explicit_roles=True` now breaks older flows. we should patch SDK to accept legacy param or default to False for service-account tokens until migration completes. propose adding `legacy_role_compat=True` flag and deprecate later.

maria: draft SDK snippet to add to docs page:
```python
# temporary compatibility wrapper
client = RedwoodClient(token=SA_TOKEN, legacy_role_compat=True)
client.kms.encrypt(key_id, plaintext)
```

anne_ops: created incident ticket: INC-1769001234 and linked to the canary rollback. security-bot created thread: #inc-1769001234. :eyes:

security-bot: Incident INC-1769001234 opened by anne_ops. severity: P2. Runbook step: roll back rbac service, enable audit logs, run migration check.

ben: follow-ups (action items):
- QA: add e2e that simulates service-account KMS calls and asserts no 403 (CI job).
- Infra: add a short-lived canary that exercises KMS with service accounts after RBAC changes.
- SDK/docs: add compatibility example + note about planned removal.
- Security: review audit log schema to ensure `actor_type` is populated for service accounts.

maria: adding a short troubleshooting blurb for internal docs (will PR): steps to check when a service account hits KMS 403 -> 1) confirm role_bindings, 2) check `rbac.migration_tags`, 3) inspect KMS audit events for actor metadata.

sanjay: once rollback is green we'll merge the migration dry-run on staging, then coordinate a canary run and SDK doc PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4231 (WIP).

anne_ops: rollback finished on canary at 14:28, error rate returned to baseline. keeping audit logging on for 30m. please comment on the PRs and notify compliance before prod migration.

maria: leaving checklist in the thread for postmortem: link to logs, migration script, SDK changes, docs updates, compliance sign-off. i'll open the PRs now. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: thanks all. we'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to walk through the migration and update the RBAC guide.
